standard_prerequisites.name: Split nodes over algebraically closed fields
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Same chapter, Definition definition-split-node and Lemma lemma-split-node
standard_prerequisites.use: Every node of X has two rational inverse images on the normalization since k is algebraically closed.

standard_prerequisites.name: The node exact sequence
standard_prerequisites.use: Supplies 0 -> O_{X,x} -> O_{X^nu,x'} (+) O_{X^nu,x''} -> k -> 0, exhibiting the completed local ring at the node inside the product of the two branches.

core_obligations: Node algebra (proof lines 6927-6939): for a node x with inverse images x', x'' and uniformizers u, v on the two branches, the multicross sequence lets one view u, v in O_{X,x} with uv = 0, each annihilator of the other.

Left to right (proof lines 6941-6949): D(uv) = 0 gives v D(u) + u D(v) = 0, and the annihilator computation forces D(u) in (u) and D(v) in (v); since O_{X^nu,x'} = k + (u), D extends across the branches and fixes x' and x'', producing D' in the right-hand side.
Right to left (proof lines 6949-6952): a derivation D' fixing x' and x'' preserves the subring O_{X,x} of the product, descending to a derivation of X.
proof_roadmap: Set up the two branches with uniformizers and the node exact sequence.
Derive the annihilator constraints from the Leibniz rule applied to uv = 0.
Extend D over the branches using the k + (u) description, checking the fixed-point condition.
Reverse the argument: derivations fixing the preimages preserve the node subring.
difficulty_reason: The lemma identifies the tangent space of a nodal curve with the node-fixed derivations of its normalization (statement lines 6916-6925). The proof (lines 6927-6952) is complete: the split-node setup, the exact sequence from the multicross lemma, the Leibniz-rule annihilator computation forcing D(u) in (u), the extension over k + (u) fixing the branch points, and the converse preservation argument. Every step is present with no omissions. H2: one local algebra computation with a short converse.
